title: DC-area forecast: Muggy this evening, mostly dry Friday and Saturday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Partly to mostly cloudy and humid with evening temperatures in the 70s and an isolated shower possible.

What’s next? A cold front sinks south Friday, delivering decent weather to end the workweek. The weekend is a mixed bag: cooler Saturday, then warmer and more humid Sunday with a heightened rain chance.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Just an isolated shower possible this evening as we remain humid with dew points in the low 70s. Lows range from the upper 60s to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): A weak cold front should sink south of the area. This means partly sunny skies as highs shoot for the low to mid-80s. Humid morning dew points up near 70 drop a bit by afternoon into the mid- to upper 60s. Can‘t rule out an isolated afternoon shower. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Mostly clear and cooler than tonight, thanks to decreasing humidity. Lows should range from near 60 in the cooler spots north and west, to the mid- and upper 60s in DC and other warm spots south and east. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Partly to mostly cloudy Saturday with cooler highs in the upper 70s and low 80s. A passing shower is possible Saturday evening or overnight with lows in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

A bit warmer and more humid on Sunday ahead of the next cold front. Partial sunshine leads temperatures toward the low to mid-80s as showers and a storm become likely during the afternoon or evening. Confidence: Medium

Mostly cloudy Monday and still on the humid side. The good news is it's cooler, with highs probably not getting out of the mid- and upper 70s. Some more showers are possible as well. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 17

Oppressive heat in 1991 sent temperatures to 96 degrees with extreme humidity, while in 2004 the remnants of Hurricane Ivan triggered a historic tornado outbreak across the region.

Today’s daily digit — 3/10: We're about a week past the average final day of 90-plus but could get there today, and humidity is high. It's not the September weather we dream of! | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
